explain: だ (plain) and です (polite) state that something is something. With friends you can drop だ altogether: 学生 alone means 'I'm a student'.

examples.en: I am a student.
It's rainy today.

pattern: N じゃない / じゃありません
explain: The negative of だ/です. じゃない is casual, じゃありません or ではありません polite. じゃ is the spoken form of では.

examples.en: This isn't my book.
Sam isn't a student.

pattern: N だった / でした
explain: Past tense of だ/です. Negative past: じゃなかった (casual) or じゃありませんでした (polite).

examples.en: Yesterday was a day off.
I was a student back then.

explain: は (read wa) marks what the sentence is about. Everything after it is a comment on that topic; it also contrasts: 'X, at least'.

examples.en: Yuki is a student.
Meat, I don't eat.

explain: も replaces は or が to mean 'also'. With a negative it means 'not … either'.

examples.en: I'm a student too.
Blip isn't going either.

explain: が marks the subject and points at new or specific information: who, what, which one. Question words like だれ and 何 take が, not は.

examples.en: Who came?
Yuki (is the one who) came.

explain: か at the end turns a sentence into a question, no change in word order. In casual speech, a rising の or just rising tone does the job.

examples.en: Are you Japanese?
What will you eat?

explain: の links nouns; the first describes the second. It also replaces a noun that's understood: 私の = mine.

examples.en: my robot
This is Yuki's.

explain: と joins nouns into a complete list. It's only for nouns, not for joining sentences.

examples.en: bread and coffee
Yuki and Sam came.

explain: や lists examples and implies there are more. Often ends with など (etc.).

examples.en: I bought apples, bananas and such.

t: ノートなどがあります
examples.en: There are books, notebooks and so on.

explain: と after a person means doing something together with them.

examples.en: I watched a movie with a friend.
I talk with Sam.

explain: を (read o) marks what the action is done to: eat what, read what.

examples.en: I eat bread.
I read a book.

explain: に marks a specific time: a clock time, a day of the week, a date. Relative times like 今日 and 毎日 take no に.

examples.en: I get up at seven.
I'll go on Sunday.

explain: に or へ (read e) marks where you're going. へ stresses direction, に the arrival; for N5 they're interchangeable with 行く, 来る, 帰る.

examples.en: I go to school.
I'm going back to Japan.

pattern: place に ある / いる
explain: に marks where something exists. ある is for things and plants, いる for people and animals.

examples.en: There's a book on the desk.
There's a dog in the park.

explain: で marks where an action takes place. Compare に, which marks where something simply exists.

examples.en: I study at the library.
Let's meet at the café.

explain: で also marks the tool or means: by bus, with chopsticks, in Japanese.

examples.en: I go by bus.
Please speak in Japanese.

pattern: A から B まで
explain: から = from (a place or time), まで = until, as far as.

examples.en: I work from nine to five.
I walk from the station to my house.

explain: ね seeks agreement ('isn't it?'); よ tells the listener something new. よね = 'right?' when you're fairly sure.

examples.en: Nice weather, isn't it?
This ramen is good, you know.

pattern: これ・それ・あれ・どれ
meaning: this, that, that over there, which
explain: こ = near me, そ = near you, あ = far from both, ど = which. この/その/あの/どの come before a noun; ここ/そこ/あそこ/どこ are places.

examples.en: What is this?
Where is the restroom?

explain: Adjectives ending in い conjugate themselves: 高い, 高くない (not), 高かった (was), 高くなかった (wasn't). いい is irregular: よくない, よかった.

examples.en: This book is interesting.
It was cold yesterday.

explain: Noun-like adjectives take な before a noun (きれいな花) and conjugate like nouns: きれいだ, きれいじゃない, きれいだった.

examples.en: It's a quiet town.
This park isn't pretty.

pattern: N が好き / きらい
explain: 好き and きらい are な-adjectives: the thing you like takes が. 大好き = love, 上手/下手 = good/bad at.

examples.en: I like cats.
Sam is good at cooking.

explain: Ru-verbs (食べる, 見る) drop る to conjugate; u-verbs (飲む, 行く) change their last sound. Only する and 来る are irregular.

examples.en: I eat a meal.
I drink water.

explain: The ます form is the polite present/future. Ru-verbs: 食べ+ます; u-verbs: change u→i (飲む → 飲みます); する → します, 来る → 来ます.

examples.en: I drink coffee every morning.
I'll go to Tokyo tomorrow.

explain: Negative: ます → ません (polite); plain ない form: 食べない, 飲まない (u→a), しない, 来ない. ある becomes ない.

examples.en: I don't eat meat.
I'm not going today.

explain: Past: ます → ました, ません → ませんでした. Plain past た follows the て-form sound changes: 食べた, 飲んだ, 行った, した.

examples.en: I watched a movie yesterday.
I already did my homework.

pattern: V-ましょう / V-ませんか
explain: ましょう suggests doing something together; ませんか is a softer invitation ('why don't we?').

examples.en: Let's eat together.
Would you like to watch a movie?

explain: Stem + たい = want to do. It conjugates like an い-adjective: 行きたくない, 行きたかった. Use it for yourself; for others say たがっている.

examples.en: I want to go to Japan.
I don't want to eat anything today.

explain: 欲しい is an い-adjective for wanting things. For actions use たい.

examples.en: I want a new computer.
What do you want?

explain: The て-form links actions in order: 起きて、食べて、出かけた. Sound changes for u-verbs: う/つ/る → って, む/ぶ/ぬ → んで, く → いて, ぐ → いで, す → して; 行く → 行って.

examples.en: I get up and drink coffee.
I walk to the station.

explain: て-form + ください is a polite request. Negative: ないでください = please don't.

examples.en: Please write your name here.
Please don't take photos.

meaning: is doing / is in a state
explain: て + いる is an ongoing action (食べている = eating) or a resulting state (結婚している = is married, 住んでいる = lives).

examples.en: I'm reading a book now.
I live in New York.

explain: て-form + もいい(です) gives or asks permission. ～てもいいですか = may I?

examples.en: May I sit here?
You may take photos.

explain: て + はいけない / はだめ forbids something. Casual: ちゃだめ.

examples.en: You must not smoke here.
Don't call late at night.

meaning: do things like A and B
explain: A non-exhaustive list of actions: past た + り, ending with する.

examples.en: On weekends I read books, watch movies and such.
We sang, danced and so on.

explain: Dictionary form + 前に = before. With nouns: 食事の前に.

examples.en: I brush my teeth before sleeping.
I wash my hands before meals.

explain: Past た + 後で (あとで) = after. With nouns: 授業の後で.

examples.en: I'll play after doing homework.
Let's go drinking after work.

explain: て + から = after doing A, (then) B. It stresses order more than 後で.

examples.en: I eat after washing my hands.
I'll call once I get home.

explain: から after a sentence gives the reason, and the result follows. Polite: 雨ですから.

examples.en: It's raining, so I'm not going.
It's good, so I'll have another.

explain: が or けど after a sentence means 'but'. けど is casual; both also soften a lead-in: すみませんが… 'excuse me, but…'.

examples.en: It's expensive but delicious.
I want to go, but I have no time.

meaning: a noun described by a verb
explain: Any plain-form sentence can sit right before a noun to describe it, like an English 'that/who' clause: 私が読んだ本 = the book I read.

examples.en: The movie I saw yesterday was interesting.
Who's the person talking over there?

explain: Nouns and な-adjectives take になる; い-adjectives change い → く: 寒くなる (get cold).

examples.en: I want to become a teacher.
It gradually got colder.

pattern: い → く / な → に
explain: い-adjectives become adverbs with く (早く = quickly), な-adjectives with に (静かに = quietly).

examples.en: I got up early.
Please be quiet.

explain: ある for things and plants, いる for people and animals. ある also means 'to have': 時間がある.

examples.en: There's a TV in the room.
I have two older brothers.

explain: Japanese counts with counters: ～つ (general), ～人 (people), ～枚 (flat), ～本 (long), ～冊 (books), ～匹 (small animals). Counter + verb: りんごを三つ買った.

examples.en: Three apples, please.
There are five students.

pattern: 何・だれ・どこ・いつ・どう
explain: Question words sit where the answer goes; no word order change. どうして / なぜ = why, いくら = how much, いくつ = how many.

examples.en: Who are you going with?
How much is this?

pattern: 何か・だれも・どこへも
explain: Question word + か = some-: 何か, だれか, どこか. Question word + も with a negative = no-: だれも来ない (nobody came).

examples.en: I want to eat something.
There's nobody here.

explain: でしょう (polite) and だろう (plain) guess or invite agreement. With rising tone: 'right?'.

examples.en: It will probably rain tomorrow.
You're tired, right?

explain: もう + past = already; もう + negative = not anymore. まだ + negative = not yet; まだ + positive = still.

examples.en: I've already eaten.
They haven't come yet.

explain: Stem + に + 行く/来る/帰る = go (come, return) somewhere to do something.

examples.en: I'm going to buy bread.
I came to Japan to study.

explain: Past た + ほうがいい gives advice. Negative advice: ないほうがいい.

examples.en: You'd better go to bed early.
Better not drink too much.

explain: より = than. AのほうがBより… = A is more … than B. 一番 = the most.

examples.en: Tokyo is bigger than New York.
I like summer best.

explain: Dictionary form + つもりだ = plan or intend to do. Negative: ないつもり.

examples.en: I plan to go to Japan next year.
I don't intend to buy anything today.

explain: なければならない / なければいけない = have to. Casual: なきゃ, なくちゃ.

examples.en: I have to go home now.
Gotta do my homework.

explain: Negative て + もいい = it's okay not to.

examples.en: You don't have to come tomorrow.
You don't have to eat it all.

explain: とき turns a clause into a time: 子どものとき (as a child), 寝るとき (when going to bed).

examples.en: What do you do when you're free?
When I went to Japan, I ate sushi.

explain: Stem + ながら: doing two things at once, the main action at the end.

examples.en: I study while listening to music.
Let's talk while we walk.

explain: だけ = only, just that much.

examples.en: Just one, please.
I only drank water.

explain: しか + negative = only, with a feeling that it's not enough.

examples.en: I only have 100 yen.
I can only speak a little Japanese.

explain: Past た + ことがある = have done it at some point.

examples.en: Have you ever eaten sushi?
I've never climbed Mt. Fuji.

explain: Dictionary form + ことができる = can. The shorter potential form (N4) is more common in speech.

examples.en: I can play the piano.
You can't swim here.

explain: Stem or adjective stem + すぎる = too much: 食べすぎる (overeat), 高すぎる (too expensive).

examples.en: These shoes are too expensive.
I drank too much yesterday.

explain: お (native words) and ご (Chinese-origin words) add politeness: お茶, お金, ご飯, ご家族.

examples.en: Have some tea.
Is your family well?

explain: N にします = I'll have N (choosing, ordering).

examples.en: I'll have coffee.
Which one will you go with?

pattern: どうやって / どうして
explain: どうやって asks how (method); どうして or なぜ asks why. Answer why with から or ので.

examples.en: How did you get here?
Why do you study Japanese?

explain: Friends and family use plain forms: 行く, 行かない, 行った, 行かなかった; だ for です (often dropped). Polite ます/です is for strangers and work.

examples.en: What are you doing tomorrow?
Did you watch a movie yesterday?

explain: Potential form: u-verbs change u → e + る (飲む → 飲める), ru-verbs add られる (食べられる; casually 食べれる), する → できる, 来る → 来られる. The object often takes が.

examples.en: I can speak Japanese.
I can't eat spicy food.

explain: Volitional form: ru-verbs + よう (食べよう), u-verbs u → ou (行こう), しよう, 来よう. Casual 'let's'.

examples.en: Let's go home together.
What shall we eat?

explain: Volitional + と思っている = I'm planning / thinking of doing.

examples.en: I'm thinking of going to Japan next year.
I think I'll go to bed early today.

explain: Plain form + と思う = I think. と marks what you think or say; だ is required after nouns and な-adjectives: 学生だと思う.

examples.en: I think it'll rain tomorrow.
I think this movie is interesting.

explain: Plain form + と言う quotes speech. Exact words go in 「」 with と.

examples.en: The teacher said there's a test next week.
Yuki said, 'I'll go right away.'

explain: って is the casual と言う / という: '…, they said', or 'something called…'.

examples.en: Sam says he's not coming.
What's this 'Blip'?

explain: Xという Y = a Y called X: 『ヨム』というアプリ.

examples.en: I use an app called Yomu.
What's this flower called?

explain: Dictionary form + と: whenever A happens, B follows naturally. Good for directions and natural results; not for requests or wishes.

examples.en: When spring comes, the flowers bloom.
Turn right and there's the station.

explain: ば-form: u → e + ば (行けば), ru-verbs れば (食べれば), い-adjectives ければ (高ければ). States a condition and its result.

examples.en: If you hurry, you'll make it.
If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

explain: Past た + ら: if A (happens), then B; also 'when A is done, B'. The most flexible conditional, fine for requests and wishes.

examples.en: If it rains, I won't go.
Please call when you get to the station.

explain: なら picks up a topic or situation: 'if it's X (that you mean)'. Great for advice: 'if you're going to Kyoto, …'.

examples.en: If you're going to Kyoto, autumn is best.
If anyone, Sam would know.

explain: たら + どう(ですか) suggests something.

examples.en: Why don't you take a break?
Why not ask the teacher?

explain: て + みる = do it and see how it goes.

examples.en: Try this cake.
I'll try speaking in Japanese.

explain: Volitional + とする = attempt (often failing), or be just about to.

examples.en: I tried to get up but couldn't.
Just as I was about to leave, the phone rang.

explain: てしまう: finish something fully, or (more often) do something with regret. Casual: ちゃう / じゃう.

examples.en: I ate the whole cake (oops).
I forgot my wallet.

explain: て + おく = do something ahead, for later; or leave it as is. Casual: とく.

examples.en: I'll book the hotel before the trip.
Leave the window open.

explain: Transitive verb + てある: someone did it and the result is there. The thing takes が.

examples.en: A map has been put up on the wall.
The beer's been chilled.

explain: ていく = going away or changing from now on; てくる = coming toward or changing up to now. Also 'go and do, then come back': 買ってくる.

examples.en: I'll go buy water at the convenience store (and come back).
It will get colder from now on.

explain: Many verbs come in pairs: transitive (someone does it, を): ドアを開ける; intransitive (it happens, が): ドアが開く. Similar: 閉める/閉まる, つける/つく, 始める/始まる.

examples.en: Please open the door.
The door opened.

explain: あげる = I/we give to someone else. Polite down to animals/kids: やる. てあげる = do a favor for someone.

examples.en: I gave my friend a book.
I taught my sister her homework.

explain: くれる = someone gives to me or my group. てくれる = someone does me a favor.

examples.en: My mom gave me a sweater.
Sam helped me out.

explain: もらう = I receive (from に/から). てもらう = have someone do something for me.

examples.en: I got a watch from my dad.
I had Yuki teach me Japanese.

pattern: ～てくれませんか / ～てもらえませんか
explain: Polite requests built on giving verbs: てくれませんか, more polite てもらえませんか, いただけませんか.

examples.en: Could you help me a little?
Could you say that again?

explain: Stem + なさい is a firm but polite order, typical of parents and teachers.

examples.en: Go to bed now.
Listen carefully.

pattern: 命令形 (行け, 食べろ)
explain: Plain imperative: u → e (行け), ru-verbs ろ (食べろ), しろ, 来い. Rude except in signs, sports and quotes. Prohibition: dictionary form + な (行くな).

examples.en: Stop (road sign)
Don't run!

explain: ので gives a reason more softly and objectively than から. After nouns and な-adjectives: なので.

examples.en: Since it's raining, I won't go out.
I have a headache, so I'll go home.

explain: のに = although, with surprise or complaint. Nouns and な-adjectives: なのに.

examples.en: Even though we promised, they didn't come.
I studied, yet the test was hard.

explain: Dictionary form + のに (+ 使う, いい, 便利, 時間がかかる) = for the purpose of.

examples.en: This app is handy for learning kanji.
It takes ten minutes to get to the station.

meaning: in order to, for the sake of
explain: Dictionary form or N の + ために = for a goal (something you control) or for someone's benefit.

examples.en: I study Japanese in order to work in Japan.
I cook for my family.

explain: Dictionary or ない form + ように = so that (a state you can't directly control, often with potential verbs).

examples.en: Please speak loudly so we can hear.
I'll write it down so I don't forget.

explain: Dictionary/potential form + ようになる = a change in ability or habit.

examples.en: I've become able to read hiragana.
I've started running every morning.

explain: Dictionary/ない form + ようにする = try to make it a habit.

examples.en: I make sure to eat vegetables every day.
I try not to drink coffee at night.

explain: Dictionary form + ことにする = I decide to. ことにしている = it's my rule.

examples.en: I've decided to study in Japan next year.
I decided to quit drinking.

explain: ことになる = it's been decided (by others or circumstances). ことになっている = it's the rule.

examples.en: It's been decided I'll transfer to Osaka next month.
The rule here is to take off your shoes.

explain: の or こと turns a verb into a noun: 泳ぐのが好き (I like swimming). こと is more formal; the senses (見る, 聞く) take の.

examples.en: I like cooking.
My hobby is taking photos.

explain: のです / んです explains or asks for an explanation; it adds 'you see' or 'what's going on?'.

examples.en: What's the matter?
It's that I have a headache.

explain: Stem / adjective stem + そう = looks (from appearance): おいしそう, 雨が降りそう. いい → よさそう, ない → なさそう.

examples.en: This cake looks delicious!
It looks like it's about to rain.

explain: Plain form + そうだ = I heard / they say. Note the difference: 降るそうだ (I hear it'll rain) vs 降りそうだ (it looks like rain).

examples.en: I heard it'll rain tomorrow.
They say that place is good.

explain: ようだ (formal) / みたいだ (casual) = it seems, based on what you see or infer. Also 'like': 夢のよう.

examples.en: It seems nobody is here.
Yuki seems tired.

explain: らしい = apparently (from what I've heard or read). After a noun also 'typical of': 男らしい.

examples.en: Apparently those two are getting married.
Today is real spring weather.

explain: Plain form + かもしれない = might. Nouns and な-adjectives drop だ. Casual: かも.

examples.en: It might snow tomorrow.
Sam might have gone home already.

explain: はずだ = I'm fairly sure based on reasons. はずがない = there's no way.

examples.en: The package should arrive tomorrow.
That can't be.

explain: Dictionary form + べきだ = should, ought to (a moral judgment). する → すべき.

examples.en: You should keep your promises.
I should have said it sooner.

explain: Passive: u → a + れる (読まれる), ru-verbs られる, される, 来られる. The doer takes に. Japanese also uses it for being bothered: 雨に降られた (I got rained on).

examples.en: I was praised by the teacher.
This book is read all over the world.

explain: Causative: u → a + せる (行かせる), ru-verbs させる, させる (する), 来させる. Context decides 'make' or 'let'. させてください = please let me.

examples.en: My mom made me eat vegetables.
Please let me do it.

explain: Causative + passive = forced to do (unwillingly). u-verbs often shorten: 飲ませられる → 飲まされる.

examples.en: As a kid I was made to take piano lessons.
My senior made me drink.

pattern: 尊敬語 (いらっしゃる, おっしゃる)
explain: Raises the other person: special verbs いらっしゃる (be/go/come), おっしゃる (say), 召し上がる (eat), ご覧になる (see), or お + stem + になる.

examples.en: What did the president say?
Please, help yourself.

pattern: 謙譲語 (まいる, いたす)
explain: Lowers yourself: まいる (go/come), いたす (do), 申す (say), いただく (receive/eat), 拝見する (see), or お + stem + する.

examples.en: My name is Yamada.
Let me carry that for you.

meaning: be able, be ready, get built
explain: できる also means 'be completed' or 'be built': ごはんができた (dinner's ready).

examples.en: Dinner's ready!
A new shop opened in front of the station.

explain: し lists reasons or points: 'and what's more…'.

examples.en: This place is cheap and good, so I come often.
It's raining and cold, let's stay home.

explain: ない + で = without doing A, (do) B. Also 'instead of'.

examples.en: I went to school without eating breakfast.
I went out without an umbrella.

explain: ずに = ないで in writing and formal speech. する → せずに.

examples.en: I read it without using a dictionary.
They left without saying anything.

explain: Stem + やすい = easy to do; + にくい = hard to do. Both conjugate as い-adjectives.

examples.en: This pen is easy to write with.
This kanji is hard to remember.

explain: Stem + 始める (begin), 終わる (finish), 続ける (keep doing), 出す (burst out).

examples.en: It started to rain.
Have you finished reading this book?

pattern: V-るところ / V-ているところ / V-たところ
meaning: about to / in the middle of / just did
explain: ところ pins a moment: dictionary form = about to, ている = in the middle of, た = just did.

examples.en: I'm just about to head out.
I just got home.

explain: Past た + ばかり = just did, it feels recent (could be days ago).

examples.en: I just came to Japan.
I just ate, but I'm already hungry.

explain: まま = leaving a state unchanged: テレビをつけたまま寝た (fell asleep with the TV on).

examples.en: Please don't come in with your shoes on.
I went out with the window left open.

explain: Stem + 方 (かた) = the way of doing: 読み方 (how to read).

examples.en: Please tell me how to read this kanji.
You're good with chopsticks.

explain: Embedded yes/no question: plain form + かどうか. With question words just か: いつ来るか.

examples.en: I don't know if it's good.
Do you know what time it starts?

explain: て + ほしい = I want (someone) to do. The person takes に.

examples.en: I want Yuki to come.
I'd like you to speak more slowly.

explain: Use たがる for others' wants (you can't know their feelings directly): 行きたがっている.

examples.en: The kids want to play outside.
My little brother wants to buy a game.

explain: Adjective stem + がる = shows signs of feeling: 寒がる, こわがる, ほしがる.

examples.en: The cat is scared of water.
Sam always acts cold.

pattern: A は B ほど～ない
meaning: A is not as … as B
explain: ほど + negative = not as much as.

examples.en: Today isn't as cold as yesterday.
Japanese isn't as hard as I thought.

explain: AはBと同じ = A is the same as B; と違う = different from.

t: のかばんはゆきさんの
examples.en: My bag is the same as Yuki's.
Japanese breakfast is different from American.

pattern: N みたいな / のような
explain: Nみたいな N / Nのような N = something like N: 夢みたいな話.

examples.en: Sounds like a dream.
I want to be someone like Yuki.

explain: Adjective stem + さ = the degree of: 高さ (height), 大きさ (size), 便利さ.

examples.en: How tall is this mountain?
The size is different.

explain: かな (casual) / かしら (feminine) = I wonder. Adds a soft guess or request: 手伝ってくれるかな?

examples.en: I wonder if it'll be sunny tomorrow.
Is this okay, I wonder?

explain: においがする, 音がする, 味がする, 気がする (I have a feeling).

examples.en: Something smells good.
I feel like someone came.

pattern: N にする / い-adj くする
explain: Nにする = make into / choose; adjective くする = make it more…: 部屋をきれいにする, 音を小さくする.

examples.en: Please turn the volume down.
I tidied up the room.

explain: でも after a noun = 'or something' (お茶でも飲みませんか) or 'even'. Question word + でも = any-: だれでも, いつでも.

examples.en: How about some tea or something?
Come any time.

explain: も after an amount stresses that it's a lot: 三時間も (a whole three hours).

examples.en: I waited a whole three hours.
I ate as many as five cakes.

explain: くらい / ぐらい = about (an amount), or 'to the extent that'.

examples.en: It's about ten minutes to the station.
I'm so happy I could cry.

explain: までに = by (no later than); まで = until (continuously).

examples.en: Please submit it by Friday.
I work until five.

explain: 間 (あいだ) = throughout a period; 間に = at some point during it.

examples.en: I was home the whole summer vacation.
It snowed while I was asleep.

explain: うちに = while the state lasts: 熱いうちに食べて (eat it while it's hot); ないうちに = before.

examples.en: Eat it while it's hot.
Let's go home before it gets dark.

explain: ば + よかった = regret: if only I had. Negative: なければよかった.

examples.en: I should have left earlier.
I wish I hadn't said that.

explain: Repeat the verb/adjective: ば-form + dictionary form + ほど.

examples.en: The more you practice, the better you get.
The more I think, the less I understand.

explain: て + も = even if; たとえ adds emphasis. Nouns: でも.

examples.en: Even if it rains, I'll go.
Even if it's expensive, I want to buy it.

explain: てもかまわない = it's no problem if (more formal than てもいい).

examples.en: Do you mind if I sit here?
It's fine if you're late.

explain: ない stem + ざるを得ない (える) = can't help but, forced by circumstances. する → せざるを得ない.

examples.en: Because of the rain, we have no choice but to cancel.
It's work, so I have to go.

meaning: the only thing to do is
explain: Dictionary form + しかない = there's no other option.

examples.en: The last train's gone, so we can only walk.
Nothing to do but go for it!

explain: わけだ = so that's why / it follows that.

examples.en: If you lived there ten years, no wonder your Japanese is good.
So that's why it's cold. The window's open.

explain: わけがない = it's impossible that.

examples.en: There's no way it's that cheap.
There's no way Sam would forget.

explain: わけではない = not necessarily; softens a denial.

examples.en: It's not that I dislike it, I just don't eat it much.
It's not that I understand everything.

explain: Dictionary form + わけにはいかない = I can't, it wouldn't be right.

examples.en: I promised, so I can't not go.
I can't drink at work.

explain: に違いない = I'm certain (from evidence).

examples.en: That person must be a teacher.
Yuki must be tired.

explain: だろうと思う = I suppose, a guess with some reasoning.

examples.en: I suppose the exam will be hard.
He's probably arrived already.

explain: っぽい = has the feel of, tends to: 子どもっぽい (childish), 忘れっぽい (forgetful).

examples.en: This bag looks cheap.
I've been forgetful lately.

explain: Stem / noun + がち = tends to (usually something undesirable): 遅れがち, 病気がち.

examples.en: In winter I tend to stay indoors.
That bus tends to be late.

explain: Stem / noun + 気味 (ぎみ) = slightly, a bit: かぜ気味 (a bit of a cold).

examples.en: I have a slight cold, so I'll sleep early.
I've been putting on a bit of weight.

explain: Noun + だらけ = full of something unwanted: まちがいだらけ.

examples.en: This essay is full of mistakes.
My shoes got all muddy.

explain: ついでに = do B taking the chance while doing A.

examples.en: While shopping, I stopped by the bookstore.
Could you mail this letter while you're out?

explain: Dictionary form / N の + たびに = every time.

examples.en: Every time I hear this song, I remember summer.
I take photos every trip.

explain: Past た + とたん(に) = the instant A happened, B (unexpected) happened.

examples.en: The moment I stood up, I got dizzy.
As soon as I opened the door, the cat jumped out.

explain: Stem + 次第 (しだい) = as soon as A, B (polite, for plans).

examples.en: I'll contact you as soon as I arrive.
We'll start as soon as we're ready.

explain: ているうちに = while doing A, B happened gradually.

examples.en: While we talked, we became friends.
I fell asleep while reading.

meaning: as (one changes, so does the other)
explain: Dictionary form / N + につれて = as A changes, B changes too.

examples.en: As you get older, time feels faster.
As my Japanese improved, it got more fun.

explain: によって = by (an agent, in passive), depending on, or because of.

examples.en: Ways of thinking differ from person to person.
This temple was built by a famous carpenter.

explain: によると / によれば = according to (source), often with そうだ.

examples.en: According to the forecast, it'll be sunny tomorrow.
According to the news, there was an accident.

explain: について = about (a topic). Before a noun: についての.

examples.en: I'm researching Japanese culture.
What do you think about this problem?

explain: に対して = toward someone/something, or in contrast.

examples.en: Speak politely to customers.
The older brother is tall, while the younger is short.

explain: にとって = for someone, as they see it.

examples.en: For me, family matters most.
For students, this book is too expensive.

explain: として = in the role or capacity of.

examples.en: I work as an interpreter.
I take photos as a hobby.

explain: に比べて (くらべて) = compared with.

examples.en: Compared to last year, this year is hot.
Compared to Tokyo, it's quiet here.

pattern: ～ばかりでなく / だけでなく
explain: だけでなく / ばかりでなく A も = not only but also.

examples.en: I can speak not only English but also Japanese.
It's not only cheap but tasty too.

explain: ばかり = nothing but, only (too much of one thing). て-form + ばかりいる = do nothing but.

examples.en: My little brother does nothing but play games.
Don't eat only meat.

explain: さえ = even (surprising extreme). さえ～ば = if only: 時間さえあれば.

examples.en: I can't even read hiragana.
If only I had time, I could go.

explain: こそ emphasizes: 今年こそ = this year for sure; こちらこそ = it's I who (should thank you).

examples.en: This year for sure, I want to go to Japan.
The pleasure is mine.

explain: なんか / なんて = something like, with a light, dismissive or surprised tone.

examples.en: Someone like me still has a long way to go.
Sam cooking? What a surprise!

explain: というか / っていうか corrects or rephrases.

examples.en: It's more cute than pretty.
I mean, it's already late.

explain: ということは = so that means.

examples.en: The lights are off. That means nobody's home.
Full means we have to wait for the next train.

explain: Dictionary form + ことだ = the best thing is to (advice).

examples.en: If you want to get good, practice every day.
Don't push yourself.

meaning: used to; that's how it is
explain: た + ものだ = used to (nostalgic); dictionary form + ものだ = that's the nature of things.

examples.en: As a kid I'd often swim in this river.
Time sure flies.

explain: Potential + ものなら = if I could (unlikely).

examples.en: If only I could, I'd be young again.
I'd go if I possibly could.

explain: た + つもり = I thought I did (but maybe not).

examples.en: I thought I'd locked it.
I meant to explain it; did it make sense?

explain: Dictionary/ない form + ように言う (頼む, 注意する) = tell (ask, warn) someone to do.

examples.en: The doctor told me not to drink.
Please tell Yuki to come.

explain: ますように = a wish or prayer.

examples.en: I hope I pass.
May it be a good year.

explain: Volitional + としない = won't even try to.

examples.en: My brother refuses to eat vegetables.
Nobody would help.

explain: Stem + かけ(る) = started but not finished: 読みかけの本 (a half-read book).

examples.en: There's a half-eaten piece of bread.
They started to say something and stopped.

explain: Stem + きる = do all the way: 使いきる (use up), 読みきる; きれない = can't finish.

examples.en: I read the whole book in one day.
I can't eat all this.

explain: Stem + 続ける = continue doing.

examples.en: We kept walking for three hours.
I want to keep studying Japanese.

explain: Stem + 出す = burst into, start suddenly: 泣き出す, 降り出す.

examples.en: The baby suddenly burst into tears.
It started raining.

explain: Stem + 直す = do over, correct: 書き直す.

examples.en: I rewrote the essay.
Please reconsider.

explain: Stem + 合う = do to each other: 話し合う (discuss), 助け合う.

examples.en: Let's talk it over together.
We help each other as a family.

explain: Causative + ていただく = humbly do something (with permission).

examples.en: We'll be closed today.
Allow me to explain.

explain: お + stem + になる raises the other person (お待ちになる); お + stem + する lowers yourself (お待ちする). お～ください = please (honorific).

examples.en: The president has already gone home.
Please wait a moment.

pattern: ございます / でございます
explain: ございます = あります (very polite); でございます = です in service speech.

examples.en: The restroom is over there.
Do you have any questions?

explain: The passive form also works as a light honorific: 先生が来られました (the teacher came).

examples.en: What time will the teacher come?
The president spoke.

explain: Stem + っぱなし = left in a state (carelessly): 開けっぱなし.

examples.en: You left the lights on.
I'm tired from standing all day.

explain: はずだった = it was supposed to (but didn't).

examples.en: The train was supposed to arrive at nine.
This isn't how it was supposed to go.

explain: ように見える = appears to be (visually).

examples.en: Yuki looks like she's having fun.
This painting looks like a photo.

pattern: ～かと思うと / かと思ったら
explain: た + かと思ったら = no sooner had A happened than B (surprising).

examples.en: Just when it cleared up, it's raining again.
No sooner did they get home than they went out.

explain: に限る = X is the best (for this).

examples.en: On a hot day, nothing beats a beer.
When you're tired, sleep is best.

explain: おかげで = thanks to (good result); せいで = due to (bad result, blame).

examples.en: Thanks to my teacher, I passed.
The game was canceled because of the rain.

explain: からこそ = it's exactly because of this.

examples.en: It's precisely because I care that I'm strict.
Because it was hard, I'm all the happier.

explain: Dictionary form + まい = won't (resolution) / probably won't (written).

examples.en: I'll never lie again.
He probably won't come.

explain: ものの = although (written). Something happened, but the result isn't as expected.

examples.en: I bought it, but I haven't used it yet.
I promised, but it looks like I can't go.

explain: にしては = considering it's X, surprisingly…

examples.en: That's good for a first time.
It's warm for December.

explain: とおり = exactly as: 言ったとおり, 説明のとおりに.

examples.en: Do it exactly as the teacher said.
Just as I thought, it started raining.

explain: ため(に) after a past/noun can mean 'because of' in formal writing.

examples.en: The train is delayed due to an accident.
School is closed because of heavy snow.

explain: にもかかわらず = in spite of (formal のに).

examples.en: Despite the rain, many people came.
Despite the warning, they were late again.

explain: かわりに = instead of, or in return for.

examples.en: I'll go instead of my mom.
In exchange for teaching English, I get taught Japanese.

explain: せいか = perhaps because (unsure cause).

examples.en: Maybe from lack of sleep, I have a headache.
Maybe it's age, but I tire easily.

explain: において = で in formal writing: 会議において.

examples.en: The conference will be held in Tokyo.
English education in Japan

explain: である is the written, essay-style だ.

examples.en: Tokyo is the capital of Japan.
This is an important problem.
